id_family: SH-DIAL, SH-USER, SH-ERR, SH-EXP, SH-GATE, SH-SEC, SH-CORE (validation; IDs stable, new IDs only for a new failure class)
label: Held-out round: POSIX sh and bash scripts
brief:
Purpose: the drafting gate. Run every POSIX/bash MUST rule and check over fresh trees the program has never read, and decide per family whether the round is clean.
Trees: about 12 blob-less depth-1 clones under /home/mherwig/.cache/research-lang/heldout/shell/<owner>__<repo> (on disk, never /tmp). Candidates: asdf-vm/asdf, dokku/dokku, tfutils/tfenv, nodenv/nodenv, dylanaraps/neofetch, pi-hole/pi-hole, GameServerManagers/LinuxGSM, Bash-it/bash-it, kubernetes/kubernetes (sparse hack/), void-linux/void-packages (sparse common/), syndbg/goenv, sdkman/sdkman-cli. Exclude every repo in shell-audit/scratch/exemplar-shas.md (the 41-repo corpus) and everything under /home/mherwig/dev. Record SHAs.
Tools: ST/run.sh toolchain (ShellCheck 0.11.0, shfmt 3.13.1); /home/mherwig/.cache/research-lang/shell-tools/matrix.sh families posix and bash.
Run:
(1) The shell-gate.sh logic of shell-gate.md, using the four-key rc (topic map X51: no check-extra-masked-returns).
(2) Every inline cell of shell-dialect.md, shell-errexit.md, shell-expansion.md, shell-gate.md, shell-security.md (the 17-cell block) and SH-CORE-07's tells. Translate first any cell still in the banned dialect (X52): git-fed lists, grep -H -n -E -e, no -r/--include/-P/$'..', PREFLIGHT line, pass = empty stdout and stderr.
(3) The SH-ERR-31 empty-glob check over every glob loop found. Its evidence today is 7 fleet loops.
(4) matrix.sh posix on 3 sampled #!/bin/sh scripts and matrix.sh bash (3.2 and 5.3) on 3 sampled bash scripts.
Classify every finding:
(i) An instance of an existing ID and failure class.
(ii) A check false positive or false negative. This gets a cell amendment, re-run red on a plant and green on a twin.
(iii) A new failure class. This gets a candidate rule with a plant/twin run.
Report per-ID hit counts, and the false-positive rate for listing cells from a read sample.
Decide: clean or not clean per family. Name the amendment and the ID for each item in (ii) and (iii). Fixtures go under shell-tools/fixtures/heldout-posix-scripts/.

label: Revision: variable-carried secrets, credential forms, names outside bash
brief:
Revision of shell-security.md. IDs SH-SEC-01..12 stay stable; any new rule takes SH-SEC-13 or above.
Three questions, each load-bearing:
(1) Completeness of SH-SEC-02's check. A secret that reaches argv through a variable is invisible to s02-argv. Examples: h="Authorization: Bearer $T"; curl -H "$h"; args+=(-H "...$T"); a URL with userinfo built in a variable. Write checks/secret-argv.sh as a two-pass awk script: pass 1 marks variables assigned from secret-named sources, pass 2 flags their use in curl, wget, git, docker, gh or cargo argv. It follows the SH-GATE-30/31 shape: awk only, exit map 0/1/69/74/78/79. Watch it red on plants and green on twins on GNU, busybox 1.37 and uutils (SH-GATE-33 hosts). Measure precision on the 40 corpus clones (SS/mine-argv.sh baseline), on the fleet, and on heldout/shell trees if present (do not wait for them). Decide: MUST cell or listing cell.
(2) Credential remedy forms the rule recommends but never ran (security Q1). Cover git through GIT_ASKPASS, credential.helper store/cache and an http.extraHeader passed through the environment, against userinfo URLs, checking .git/config persistence and /proc/<pid>/cmdline. Cover cargo login reading the token on stdin and CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN in the environment, against a stub alternative registry. Run each on the matrix and record what argv shows.
(3) The scope of SH-SEC-09 outside bash. Run local "$k=v", typeset -n, read "$k" and printf-style dynamic names on dash, busybox ash, mksh, ksh93u+m, yash, posh and zsh, via matrix.sh posix and zsh.
Fixtures go under shell-tools/fixtures/shell-security-rev/. Decide amendments by ID, and log them in a Revision log section.

brief:
Revision of shell-emit.md. IDs SH-EMIT-01..50 stay stable. Rows that belong to SH-NU and SH-ELV are handed to shell-alt-shells.md by pointer, not edited.
(1) ble.sh. SH-EMIT-24 and SH-EMIT-43 are MUST rules, and their ble.sh clauses were measured on one nightly (0.4.0-nightly+d81fd54, bash 5.2.21). Build the latest tagged ble.sh release and the current nightly. Re-run FR/hooks/bash/twin.sh with ble-attach before and after, sourced once and twice, plus the blehook PRECMD and CHPWD forms, on bash 5.2 and 5.3. Decide: the clauses hold on the release, or they are scoped to 'nightly as of <date>'.
(2) pwsh 7.6 Windows rows (emit subarea 1b). Run on the Windows host via matrix.sh pwsh and win, staged only under C:\Users\ecom\shell-wintest. Never write the owner's real $PROFILE or registry. Resolve profile paths per edition read-only, and run the rc-edit harness against copied profile files under the staging dir. Cover: completion registration read-back (SH-EMIT-33, 38, 39; Register-ArgumentCompleter, -NativeFallback on 7.6.6 and 5.1); LocationChangedAction combined through [Delegate]::Combine and the 5.1 prompt wrapper (SH-EMIT-42); the env and data channel rows (SH-EMIT-06, 07: empty $env:X, base64 payload).
(3) Windows config paths for nu and elvish. Use portable nu 0.116.1 and elvish 0.21.0 staged in the same dir with config locations redirected into staging. Measure $nu.data-dir/vendor/autoload (SH-EMIT-17, SH-NU-07) and the rc.elv location (emit subarea 1c).
Decide per row: confirmed, scoped, or amended. Log every change in the Revision log. Fixtures go under shell-tools/fixtures/shell-emit-rev2/.
